bottleneck: Between 2002 and 2021 over 100 amyloid-targeting drug candidates failed, and a 2026 Cochrane review of 17 trials in 20,000 patients found anti-amyloid antibodies clear plaques without meaningful cognitive benefit. Thirty percent of cognitively normal elderly carry heavy plaque burden, and plaque density correlates weakly with symptoms — unlike tau. The field's dominant hypothesis may mistake a marker, or even a protective response, for the cause.
current_state: Lecanemab and donanemab are approved but with marginal benefit and brain-bleed risks; the UK and France declined coverage. Research is pivoting to tau, inflammation, and vascular factors.

title: Amyloid hypothesis fails to explain Alzheimer's
why_it_blocks: Decades and billions were spent on a hypothesis that clears plaques without restoring minds. Until the true causal chain is found, Alzheimer's drug development is shooting in the dark.
